exposure: Primary meconium-stained amniotic fluid (MSAF) (present at membrane rupture)
Secondary meconium-stained amniotic fluid (MSAF) (transitioned from clear to MSAF during labor)
cohort: The study included 4302 deliveries from a total of 30,215, all at or beyond 37 weeks gestational age, between October 2008 and July 2018, comparing those with primary MSAF to those with secondary MSAF.
finding: Secondary meconium-stained amniotic fluid (MSAF) was associated with a higher rate of composite adverse neonatal outcomes compared to primary MSAF.
mod_finding: The secondary MSAF group had higher rates of cesarean deliveries and assisted vaginal deliveries.
